report.summary: Two separate root causes. The app's list_books ignores the owner, so every user sees every user's books, which fails the API isolation test and the new-user empty-state UI test; fix that in app/main.py first. The two UI add-book tests fail because pages.py clicks the test id "add-books" while the template renders "add-book", which is a test-side locator bug that needs a one-line fix.

causes.title: Book list is not filtered by owner, so users see each other's books
causes.explanation: list_books(user_id) takes the user id but never uses it. The query selects every row in the books table, so any logged-in user gets all books. Per-user lookups (get_own_book) are correctly scoped, which is why GET/DELETE of another user's book returns 404 and only the listing leaks. In the UI test, the freshly registered user's page shows rows created by other tests in the same session-scoped database, so the empty-state element is absent. The tests are right to expect isolation and an empty shelf for a new user.
evidence: app/main.py:147-150: def list_books(user_id: int) -> list[dict]: with db() as conn: rows = conn.execute("SELECT * FROM books ORDER BY id").fetchall()  (no owner_id filter)
app/main.py:163-166: get_own_book filters with "WHERE id = ? AND owner_id = ?", so the scoping exists for single-book access but not for listing
tests/api/test_books_api.py:41-42: other_ids = [b["id"] for b in other_api.list_books().json()]; assert book["id"] not in other_ids
Failure: assert 2 not in [1, 2]. The other user's listing contains the first user's book id

Login UI failure aria snapshot shows the new user's table with rows "Final title Someone 2001" and "From API-7eba9a2e Robot", which belong to other tests, and no data-testid="empty-state" element (tests/ui/test_login_ui.py:14)
tests/conftest.py:31-56: base_url is session-scoped, so one database is shared by all tests in the session
causes.suggested_fix: In list_books, add "WHERE owner_id = ?" with user_id, e.g. conn.execute("SELECT * FROM books WHERE owner_id = ? ORDER BY id", (user_id,)). Then rerun both tests.

causes.title: Page object clicks test id 'add-books', but the template uses 'add-book'
causes.explanation: BooksPage.add in tests/support/pages.py clicks get_by_test_id("add-books"). The books template renders the submit button with data-testid="add-book". The locator never matches, so Playwright times out after 5 s before the form is submitted. The app is behaving correctly here; the page object is stale. Both UI tests that use BooksPage.add fail at this line. Once the click works, the future-year test's remaining assertions look consistent with books_add, which returns a 422 error and keeps the form values, but I did not run them.
evidence: Failure: Locator.click: Timeout 5000ms exceeded. Call log: - waiting for get_by_test_id("add-books")
Aria snapshot in the login test shows the button as 'button "Add book"', confirming the element exists but without the expected test id
causes.suggested_fix: Change tests/support/pages.py:44 to get_by_test_id("add-book"), or change the template to data-testid="add-books" if that name is the intended contract. Prefer fixing the page object, since other locators use the template's names. Then rerun the two UI add-book tests.
